title: sticky-route-entanglement-kv-staleness-triggered-cross-region-amplification
creator: Asha Patel
description: During a peak-capacity window on 2026-02-27 we observed a cross-region reroute spiral where requests pinned to stale sticky-route state repeatedly retried across region boundaries. The tenant-facing symptom was elevated latency and request amplifications; internal telemetry showed KV cache shard staleness combined with policy precedence inversion created an entangled decision graph that prevented graceful fallback. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, short-term mitigations already applied, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-27T02:14Z - First alert: increased 95th latency for generation endpoints in eu-west, service error rate +4%
2026-02-27T02:19Z - Router traces show increasing cross-region retries; tenants were bounced between eu-west and us-central repeatedly
2026-02-27T02:30Z - Incident declared; mitigation: temporarily increased routing backoff and enforced sticky-route TTL refresh to break loops
2026-02-27T03:05Z - Short-term fix deployed: force-evict stale KV shards for affected policies and lowered policy propagation TTL from 30s->8s for hot shards
2026-02-27T04:00Z - Service stabilized; latency returned to baseline but telemetry indicates some requests still experienced variant mismatch fallbacks
2026-02-28T10:00Z - Post-incident kickoff meeting with runtime, router, and infra teams to triage root cause and action items
root_cause: A race between policy propagation and KV shard eviction led to inconsistent 'sticky-route' state across router replicas. When a routing policy change (weight/variant updates) coincided with a capacity-rebalancing event, some router replicas served stale route entries while others saw updated precedence. The decision graph became entangled: requests were routed to a secondary region because the local variant was marked unavailable, then retried back to primary where a stale sticky key forced the same decision repeatedly. The underlying trigger was twofold: (1) insufficient KV shard invalidation guarantees during rebalancing and (2) precedence resolution logic that preferred stale affinity over recent policy snapshots when TTLs diverged.
mitigations: Immediate: forced KV shard eviction for affected customers (completed 2026-02-27 03:05Z)
Immediate: lowered policy propagation TTL for hot policy shards to reduce window of divergence (temporary)
Short-term: added a safety backoff on cross-region retries to make loops self-terminating and reduce amplification
Monitoring: add an alert for 'sticky-route rebind rate' and for sustained variant mismatch errors across regions
action_items: (Luca) Implement consistent KV shard invalidation API: atomic invalidate-and-confirm for policy snapshots - ETA 2026-03-11
(Runtime) Add deterministic precedence tie-breaker that prefers the most recent policy snapshot timestamp across replicas - ETA 2026-03-09
(Routing) Introduce loop-detection token per-request and circuit-breaker that trips after 3 cross-region handoffs; record metric 'cross_region_handoff_count' - ETA 2026-03-04 (in progress)
(Infra) Expand canary rollout to simulate policy rebalancing under load in staging (include synthetic kv-stale scenarios) - ETA 2026-03-15
(SRE) Create a runbook entry: 'sticky-route entanglement' with step-by-step eviction, telemetry queries, and rollback steps - ETA 2026-03-06
(Observability) Dashboard: build page showing per-policy propagation latency, KV shard staleness histogram, and cross-region retry amplification - ETA 2026-03-10
(QA) Add fuzz tests that inject out-of-order policy snapshots and KV invalidation delays into the router decision path - ETA 2026-03-12
(Product) Evaluate policy propagation defaults and surface a 'safe-mode' for enterprise tenants to opt into conservative TTLs during heavy changes - ETA 2026-03-20
